# Second-pass review — CDSFL @ `8879c34`

**Tree verified first, as instructed.** `git rev-parse HEAD` → `8879c3450380247ae66985ff3fbfc582f35a8c20`; `git status --short` → empty. The harness carried the work; this review is of the committed tree.

**Suite:** `4496 passed, 11 skipped, 4 failed in 380.88s`. The brief predicted 4493/7/0. **All four failures are sandbox artefacts, and I proved it rather than assumed it** — see §6. My first read of one of them was "genuine"; the check refuted me.

## 1. The table, item by item

**#1 directive path — the fix is real but lands at a layer this runner never reads. This is my main disagreement.**

`system_prompt_path` appears nowhere in `reference_runner_v2.py` or `runner_core.py`:

```
Grep "system_prompt_path" bench/*.py
→ experiment_11_orchestrator.py (a different runner), smoketest, run_confer_smoke, test_falsifier_matrix
```

The file that *does* get read is loaded at `reference_runner_v2.py:11972`, and AST places that line inside **`main()` (11961–12046)** — the CLI route. The harness bypasses `main()` and calls `run_experiment(exp_cfg, "", cfg)` directly. Inside `run_experiment`, `cdsfl_text` is the parameter, never reassigned, passed straight to `_dispatch_round_star` (10414–10416) → `_dispatch_single_model` (7002–7005).

And the composed directive does not carry the core text either — 6 distinctive ≥60-char lines from `cdsfl_core_formal.md`, checked against each composition: **0/6 present for every model.**

So the 26,909-char core directive still reaches no simulated model. The FATAL guard correctly stops a *wrong path* being swallowed, but the path was never the delivery mechanism here. **The repair that actually fixed the empty-prompt failure was #4** (`base_model_label` at 6774), not #1. The commit message's causal story — "an `is_file()` guard turned that into a silent None … the simulated panel received NO CDSFL directive" — has the right symptom and the wrong mechanism.

**#2 transport-dead — TRUE, and it survived my attempt to break it.** I tried three ways:

- *Does hoisting change `error_routed` semantics?* `error_routed` is read at exactly one site, `4578`, inside the sub-critical branch. Grep confirms the only other occurrences are tests and `replay_routing_on_control.py`.
- *Can a critical be demoted to sub-critical and then be wrongly skipped by its new `error_routed=True`?* Severity is mutated at exactly one site, `5492` in `_calibrate_finding_severity`, which requires `falsifier_verdict == "CONFIRMED"` (5467). `"CONFIRMED" not in ROUTABLE_INSTRUMENT_FAULTS` (`frozenset({'ERROR','UNTOOLABLE','NON_DISCRIMINATING'})`), so such an entry is skipped at 4577 for the *verdict* reason regardless. Inert, as the comment claims.
- *Sub-critical one-attempt semantics?* The 4577 guards `continue` before line 4601 is reached, so nothing changes for sub-criticals.

The repair is correct. I could not falsify it.

**#3 discrimination overlay — TRUE.**
```
_build_discrimination_overlay(REPO, "bench/dm/_memory.py", src)  → OK
_build_discrimination_overlay(REPO, "<abs>/bench/dm/_memory.py", src)
  → ValueError: discrimination control: target must be repo-relative
```

**#4 composer — TRUE for 5 of 6, and the sixth matters more than the brief says.** `base_model_label` strips `-SIM` correctly, and CC2/DeepSeek/Gemini/Codex/ChatGPT compose (6,787 / 3,731 / 6,787 / 3,731 / 6,787 chars). **`Fable-SIM` → `Fable` → no `COMPOSER_MODEL_MAP` entry → no `Fable.toml` → `FileNotFoundError` → `model_cdsfl = cdsfl_text` = `""`.** The brief records that Fable has no `.toml`; it does not record the consequence, which is that 1 of 6 panellists still runs with **zero** per-model directive and, because `cdsfl_text` is `""`, zero core directive — briefed by the operational directive alone.

**#5 `discrimination_control_ask` — TRUE.** `9531` documents it as read nowhere; `9539` logs loudly if set.

**#7 rounds 7 → verification — the fix is very likely inert, and this is checkable.** `start_round = 0` (9798), `loop_cap = cfg.extension_cap = 7` (9998), so rounds are **0…6**. `_verification_step` returns `{"skipped": True}` while `round_idx < 6` (7698). That gives verification **exactly one round out of seven — the last one — and only if the run does not converge first.** `gamma_alt_earliest_round = 3`, and the v3.1 report shows `converged_at: 3`. Unless the next run fails to converge at 3, 4 *and* 5, `verified` will again be False on every entry. Raising the harness to 7 does not clear a threshold of 6 when convergence is expected at 3.

**#8 shadow cells / `test_cmd` — TRUE.** `_macrophage` is one of the sections `_run_shadow_cells` recognises; `test_cmd` is set.

**#9, #10** — accepted as stated; no independent check needed.

*Minor:* the shim docstring lists nine dispatching functions. AST finds **8 call sites in 7 enclosing functions** (`_apply_routing` and `run_experiment` appear only via the nested `resolve_fn` and `_arb_dispatch`). Harmless — patching the primitive covers all — but the number in the docstring is wrong.

## 4. What we both missed

**(a) The repairs are coupled, and #1/#4 switched on #6.** The `-SIM` fingerprints are committed at `c62d7f3`, written by the v3.1 run:

```
CC2-SIM  max_successful_prompt_chars = 35,013  (effective limit ×0.9 = 31,511)
```

That 35,013 was measured *while the composer was failing*, i.e. with a ~44K system prompt and no phenotype. Fix #4 adds 3.7–6.8K per model. Payloads now clear the fingerprint-derived limit by 2.3×. **Repairing the directive is what makes the decomposition bypass fire.** Two findings the review treated as independent are one causal chain.

Worse, those fingerprints are artefacts of a run the brief itself declares invalid — no directive, 0/19 falsifiers — and they now steer decomposition for every future simulated run. They should be deleted, not carried.

**(b) A stale docstring that argues for exactly the demotion the founder's standing directive forbids.** `_check_gamma_alt_convergence`'s docstring says:

> γ IS REPORTED, NEVER A TRIGGER OR BLOCKER (panel ruling 2026-05-23). The former γ-threshold trigger (condition 1) is DELETED

The code beneath it does the opposite, correctly:

```python
if gamma_critical < theta:
    return (False, f'two-sided gate: … BOTH sides of the gate must agree.')
```

The code honours the standing directive; the docstring above it is the most persuasive available argument for breaking it, sitting inside the function a future reader would edit. Under `docs-defect-parity` this is a defect of equal standing to a code defect.

**(c) The panel is six copies of one model.** `SHIM.install(timeout=…)` takes `model="sonnet"` by default (`sim_dispatch_shim.py:148`) for all six vendor labels, and the harness exposes no flag to vary it. `lookup_alias_any` was repaired so cross-model co-discovery can record — but co-discovery, divergence and the location-shadow machinery measured across six identical agents are structurally degenerate, not merely noisy. Whatever ρ and the divergence directive report, it is not what six frontier models would produce.

**(d) A hypothesis I tested and abandoned — reported because the negative is information.** I suspected the vacuous-curve guard (`cumulative_critical == 0 and gamma_critical < theta`) was unreachable, on the theory that γ defaults high on an empty series, which would silently suppress the `REVIEW THIS RUN: a clean target and a broken severity classifier look alike from here` warning. It does not: `_estimate_gamma([0,0,0]) → 0.0`, `_estimate_gamma([1,0,0,0]) → 1.0`. The branch is reachable and correct. The v3.1 convergence at `gamma_critical=1.000` reflects one critical found then decayed to zero — a legitimate curve, not a vacuous one.

## 5. Bench Run 2 readiness

**The falsifier integrity guard's verdict depends on where the repo is checked out.** `scan_falsifier_source(code, repo_root=None)` rejects any user-path not strictly under the repo root (`falsifier_verify.py:696–711`). Archived falsifiers that name the founder's absolute repo path are honest there and `INTEGRITY_VIOLATION` anywhere else. Measured across all 469 falsifiers in the 49 tracked reports, cross-verified with two tools:

```
all archived falsifiers   15/469 = 3.2%   Wilson[statsmodels] [1.9%, 5.2%]  Clopper-Pearson[scipy] [1.8%, 5.2%]
exp49 engineering (prose)  5/33  = 15.2%  Wilson [6.7%, 30.9%]              CP [5.1%, 31.9%]
exp48 chemistry  (prose)   2/35  =  5.7%  Wilson [1.6%, 18.6%]              CP [0.7%, 19.2%]
exp45 (_memory.py)         0     —  cannot fire at exp45 scale
```

Prose targets are where models write absolute paths, at roughly 5× the archive-wide rate. `docs/REPRODUCING.md` invites third-party replication; a third party cloning to any other path has honest falsifiers scored as integrity violations, which feeds `falsifier_verdict` → `unverified_critical_count` → convergence. **Zero occurrences on the exp45 target, so no simulated run can surface it.** This is the clearest example of the class the brief asked for.

**The decomposition hard floor is 3,431 chars away.** `DECOMPOSE_HARD_FLOOR_CHARS = 80,000`, fingerprint-independent. The system prompt alone is already **47,890–50,946 chars**. Round-0 payload on the 20,605-byte exp45 target is **76,569**; the late-round payload is **85,959**, already over. So a model with no fingerprint decomposes by mid-run *on the smallest target in the series*, and any Bench Run 2 target ~4KB larger decomposes from round 0. That route — `decomposed_dispatch`, four real backends — cannot be exercised by any simulated run, because `api="sim"` short-circuits it at the first branch.

**Two seam paths are dark in simulation but live in real configs:** `_arb_dispatch` (`merge_arbitration_enabled` False in sim, True in exp45) and `_post_convergence_sweep` (0 rounds in sim, 2 in the config the code comment at 11705 cites). The seam covers them; the *simulation* never calls them.
